subject: Private deployment maintenance: sidegrade window negotiation and runbook request (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Matt Bowers <matt.bowers@acmehealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-21T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment maintenance: initial ask

Hi Jonas / Neha,

We need to schedule a maintenance window for the Acme Health private deployment to apply the March security micro-patch and a minor runtime sidegrade. Compliance (SOC2) requires us to capture pre/post snapshots and retain rollback logs for 90 days. A few constraints on our side: we have a blackout window for reporting (2028-04-01 to 2028-04-07) so any disruptive activity must happen before that or be a true zero-delta operation.

Requests:
- Can you propose a 2–4 hour window with canary plan and rollback criteria?
- Confirm policy for tenant "version pinning" during maintenance and how long we can hold a shelved version if rollback is needed.
- We will need evidence of audit logs (requesting file list) and an estimated change in p99 latency.

Suggested times from our ops calendar: 2028-03-28 01:00–05:00 UTC (preferred) or 2028-04-02 22:00–02:00 UTC (fallback). Please advise what works for Redwood and whether a short net-drain is required.

I've attached our approval matrix for this cycle.

Thanks,
Matt Bowers
Head of Platform, Acme Health
Attachment: Acme_approval_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Matt Bowers <matt.bowers@acmehealth.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-21T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment maintenance: initial ask

Matt — thanks for the heads up and the matrix. We're aligned to be conservative on this. High level proposal below; I'll publish a formal runbook once we lock the window.

Proposal (summary):
- Preferred window: 2028-04-02 23:00–02:00 UTC (Redwood ops + Acme on bridge). Alternate: 2028-03-27 02:00–05:00 UTC. If Acme prefers the March 28 range you suggested we can accommodate but will need an earlier preflight.
- Approach: "sidegrade" (no forced model/minor runtime changes) with staged pinning:
  1) Snapshot current tenant state (config, KV cache, routing table) — retained 90 days.
  2) Apply runtime sidegrade on a canary (10% of traffic for 30 minutes).
  3) If canary passes health gates, roll to 50% and then 100% in 10–15 minute steps with warm KV rehydration.
- Pinning policy: we will pin the Acme tenant to the pre-change version for 72 hours post-deploy (shelved version available for 14 days for emergency rollback).
- Rollback criteria (automated & manual):
  • Error rate increase +2% absolute over baseline sustained for 5 minutes.
  • p99 latency exceed baseline +150ms for 10 minutes.
  • Any data-integrity or auth anomalies.
- Expected impact: optimistic — no brand-new migrations; kernel and runtime library patch are minor and will not change model weights. We anticipate p99 delta <= 50ms in steady state, canary may spike briefly during KV warms.
- Network: brief session drain recommended (30–60s) on the canary nodes; full rollback requires rebind to shelved version and force-cache-invalidation.

Compliance artifacts we will provide: pre/post snapshots (tar list), full audit log export for the window, and a signed change record.

I've attached a draft proposal PDF and will open a Jira (INF-2029) with the runbook checklist.

Can you confirm which window you prefer and who will be on the post-change review? Also confirm whether KMS rotation is in-scope for this change (we recommend not to include it in the same window).

— Jonas
VP, Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
Attachment: private_patch_proposal_v1.pdf
Related: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2029
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-21T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment maintenance: initial ask

Quick ops checklist (to be added to the runbook):
- Preflight (48 hrs): synthetic smoke tests + canary config validated, snapshot created and verified on remote object store.
- Network: ensure firewall rules + BGP next-hop remain stable; request netops to hold off any config pushes during window.
- DB/KV: create consistent snapshot, export KV key list (for small tenants like Acme we do full prefix export).
- Deployment steps: canary deploy -> warm KV -> traffic ramp -> full cutover -> 72h pin -> release after signoff.
- Abort sequence: immediate traffic split back to pre-change nodes, restore pinned version, invalidate cache, and collect failure dump for A/R.
- On-call: ops lead (Neha) + karthik on-net + irene as rollout owner. Please reply with backup names for your side.

I will draft ops_checklist_preflight.md and attach to the Jira.

— Neha
Engineering Manager, Private Deployments
From: Matt Bowers <matt.bowers@acmehealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-22T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment maintenance: sidegrade window negotiation and runbook request

Jonas / Neha — thanks, that all looks reasonable. We prefer the 2028-04-02 23:00–02:00 UTC window (ties out with our low-traffic period) and will have both platform and security leads on the bridge: myself (Matt Bowers) and Priya Desai (secops@acmehealth.com). We do NOT want KMS rotation in the same window.

Action items for Redwood:
- Publish the full runbook (INF-2029) with explicit timings and rollback kick criteria by 2028-03-28 COB.
- Share the preflight checklist and confirm the snapshot storage location (we prefer immutable object store).
- Confirm that pinned-shelved version retention is 14 days and provide process for emergency revert.

We will sign off once runbook + audit artifact templates are received. If you need a PO or formal change request we can generate it after runbook review.

Regards,
Matt Bowers
Head of Platform, Acme Health
Attachment: (none)
